objectClass.primaryType: roadside regulatory traffic sign with a supplementary plate
objectClass.notes: A 0.6 m blue-and-red prohibition disc with a white NO PARKING supplementary plate hung beneath it, both bolted to a 50 mm square hot-dip galvanised post that runs the full height of the prop and past the disc's crown.

reasoning: Silhouette is two primitives: a thin plate and a slender vertical support. Nothing organic, nothing swept.
All identity lives in the PRINTED FACE, not in geometry. That routes to a canvas atlas, not to components.
Held to 2 draw calls by the asset budget, so the post and everything sharing its material get ONE mesh between them and the plate is the other.
The diagonal slash is chiral - a slash the other way is a different sign - so the atlas must not be mirrored, which fixes the sign of the front-cap UV mapping.
The supplementary plate is folded into the disc's buffer rather than given its own component, which is the whole reason this prop fits two draw calls.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Wide red prohibition border running 1.00R to about 0.83R, read off the x=520 scanline where the border spans y 118-145 against a disc centre at 298 and a radius of 186. Trimmed to #BF6149 over 676 px on the least-shadowed upper-left arc.
Blue ground filling the disc inside the border, measured #337AB9 over 3600 px.

A SINGLE red diagonal bar across the disc running upper-left to lower-right - chirality is an identity feature here and the atlas must not mirror it, because a slash the other way is a different sign. The same paint as the border; its separate measurement of #BF7358 is the key's work, not a different red.
Two dark legend lines on the white supplementary plate, Thai over Latin NO PARKING. Ink trimmed to #303131 over 3092 sub-luma-70 px. SOLID FILL, never an outline.

Two dark hex heads on the disc's vertical centreline. Classified as a DECAL and not a fastener on purpose: in this model they are printed into the atlas and have no geometry, so calling them fasteners would claim instanced hardware that does not exist.
Mottled grey hot-dip spangle over the post. Only 186 of 3240 px in the shaft crop pass a strict neutral filter - this post is the most weathered of the eight.

Orange-brown rust over the lowest stretch of the post, arriving abruptly at a splash line. The per-band scan's 46 per cent reading at the disc's red border was discarded as the border passing the orange filter, not rust.

authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

declaredContract.rationale: A bolted roadside sign is a static rigid body. Nothing hinges, nothing turns, and nothing clips into it. One root pivot and zero sockets is the CORRECT answer, not a gap: a named pivot promises a part turns on that axis and a named socket promises something attaches there, and this prop can keep neither.
declaredContract.destructionRationale: The asset declares no destruction groups, so no component carries a fractureGroup and the prop does not come apart.

ground-termination: the post runs out of the bottom of the frame, so nothing is known about a flange. Built as a plain post rather than inventing a footplate. Confidence 0.7.

componentTree.name: Prohibition disc and supplementary plate
componentTree.topologyRationale: Two flat plates, each two parallel planar caps joined by a short wall, closed and rigid. Merged into ONE buffer because they share a material, share a plane and never move relative to one another.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 72-segment disc and a rounded-rect plate, merged into ONE BufferGeometry at build time.
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: authored - rewritten after generation into a THREE-region atlas: the disc's front cap takes the prohibition graphic, the supplementary plate's front cap takes the NO PARKING legend, and every wall and back-cap vertex collapses to a single bare-aluminium texel. Two printed faces and a plain back on ONE material and ONE draw call.
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 72 radial segments on the disc, which is where the triangles go and the only place they are spent. The circular outline IS this prop's silhouette and a visible polygon on the rim is the one defect no material work can recover. The supplementary plate gets 4 segments per corner and nothing else.

mergedAssembly.reason: maxDrawCalls is 2 and the post must have one of them, so the disc and the supplementary plate get ONE mesh between them. They share a material, sit in the same plane and never move relative to each other, so merging is invisible. Recorded as a BLOCKOUT decision so a later pass does not 'fix' the shallow tree by splitting it and silently costing every instance of this sign an extra submission.

parts.note: The 0.6 m regulatory disc, which sets the DECLARED width. Rotated so its axis lies on +Z and its caps face front and back.
The white NO PARKING plate hung under the disc. Narrower than the disc, so it does NOT set the prop's width - the reference confirms this, its 285 px against the disc's 372 px across the same view.

mergedAssembly.jointNote: The two plates share a plane at z=+0.0145 to +0.0265 but do not touch: a 0.32 m vertical gap separates the disc's bottom edge at y=1.70 from the plate's top at y=1.61. Coplanar and co-facing surfaces that do not OVERLAP cannot z-fight, which is why they may share a plane where a panel sitting flush on a wall may not.

pivot.notes: Not an articulation. Neither plate turns on anything; this is the merged component's transform origin, and the model exposes exactly ONE named pivot, the root.

collider.notes: Declared collider for this asset is `cylinder`, and the proxy is put on the DISC because the disc is what a projectile meets. The supplementary plate is inside the disc's swept footprint in plan and needs no proxy of its own.

featureReviews.evidence: 72 radial segments, 288 of the prop's 544 triangles, and the only place triangles are deliberately spent. The rim reads as a true circle at every turntable azimuth and edge-on the disc reads as a thin plate rather than a wedge.

Disc and supplementary plate merged into ONE BufferGeometry: same material, same plane, never moving relative to each other. lodPlan.strategy: as built - already below the per-draw-call overhead, so there is no far tier worth authoring
none. A decimated tier would save nothing measurable and would cost a unique geometry against a ceiling that is full.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() and none was invented. DRAW CALLS are the binding axis and triangles are not.

drawCalls.note: At the ceiling with nothing spare. maxDrawCalls was raised from 1 to 2 BEFORE any geometry existed. The obvious third component - the supplementary plate as its own mesh - was REFUSED and folded into the disc's buffer instead: it shares the disc's material and never moves relative to it, so a separate mesh would have bought nothing and cost the axis that has nothing to give.

materials.note: Two. The third was available and was NOT spent: a separate material for the white supplementary plate would have been the easy way to a blue disc and a white plate, and it would have cost a DRAW CALL as well as a material. The UV atlas is what makes one material carry a blue disc, a white plate and a bare aluminium back.

uniqueGeometries.note: One merged disc-plus-plate buffer and one segmented box. Both are built once at module scope, and so is the atlas canvas - every instance shares all three.

triangles.note: The disc's 72 radial segments are 288 triangles and the only place triangles are deliberately spent: the circular outline is this prop's silhouette. The supplementary plate is a 20-point extrusion at 76. The post is a box at 14 height segments, spent to carry the rust ramp without a texture. The 320 spare are NOT spent - the two face bolts are the obvious candidate and they stay PRINTED, because at 14 mm they are under a pixel at prop distance.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: The disc's blue field reads 100-106 on its upper-left arc against 118-124 lower-right, and the red slash reads #BF7358 where the border reads #BF6149 - a soft key, high and camera-left, lifting the lower-right of the disc.
The disc's rim return stays at luma 151 where it turns away from the key, which only happens with real fill rather than a single source.
A thin bright line separates the disc's upper-right arc from the backdrop.
